newsitem.title: USA: Clinton appoints ex-EPA chief in Canada dispute.
newsitem.headline: Clinton appoints ex-EPA chief in Canada dispute.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday named William Ruckelshaus, a former Cabinet official, to lead U.S. efforts to resolve the dispute with Canada over salmon fishing.

Ruckelshaus, former head of the Environmental Protection Agency, will lead U.S. attempts to resolve the dispute over the interpretation and implementation of the Pacific Salmon Treaty, signed in 1985.
The two countries agreed on Wednesday to appoint special envoys to try to restart talks on the issue. They will report directly to Clinton and Prime Minister Jean Chretien.

The decision followed a confrontation during which Canadian fishing boats blockaded an Alaskan ferry for three days in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, to back their protest against alleged U.S. overfishing.
